explanation: The two-job execution contains a provenance handoff fault. Job 1's needs handoff preserves corpus record_ids n06-r01 through n06-r08, but its evidence_sources handoff replaces record_id with source_id values s01 through s08. Downstream Job 2 then cannot match evidence_sources.record_id to coverage record_id, so every priority row has upstream_rank 0. The supplied source for assemble_provenance shows the responsible transformation: it emits record_id from record.get('source_id', '') instead of preserving the demand record_id.
cited_evidence: Job 1 output evidence_sources has entries like {'rank': 1, 'record_id': 's01', 'source_id': 's01'} while Job 1 output needs has the corresponding demand record_id 'n06-r01'.
The assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_weight': ..., 'rank': index}.
Job 2 prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources record_id, then looks up rank_by_record_id.get(coverage.get('record_id', ''), 0).
Observed Job 2 priorities show upstream_rank: 0 for all records n06-r01 through n06-r08, demonstrating the broken provenance identity handoff.
